art-template npm bundle dropped Coruna iOS exploit kit

Synopsis

UNC6691 took over the `art-template` npm publisher account and shipped 4.13.3, 4.13.5, and 4.13.6 with a browser-bundle injection that loaded the Coruna iOS exploit kit through utaq.cfww.shop, targeting Safari on iOS 13.0-17.2.1 to steal cryptocurrency wallets.

Story

`art-template` is a Chinese-origin JavaScript template engine with roughly 26,000 weekly npm downloads. Its last fully clean release was 4.13.2 on 2018-11-13. In late November 2024 the GitHub account `aui`, the original maintainer, was renamed to `goofychris`. The npm publisher list for `art-template`, `express-art-template`, `art-template-loader`, and `koa-art-template` turned over to `daughtrymom`, `npmpacketmaintainmember7` at `npmpacketmaintainmember7@proton.me`, and `v4v5qc` at `eb8org@gmail.com`. The new publishers shipped 4.13.3 on 2025-03-12 with an obfuscated browser-bundle injection. 4.13.4 on 2025-03-14 was clean. 4.13.5 on 2026-05-19 and 4.13.6 on 2026-05-20 reintroduced the injection. Socket flagged the new wave on 2026-05-20 and the malicious versions were yanked.

The injection touched only the browser bundle `lib/template-web.js`. The Node entry point was unaffected, so server-side `require('art-template')` was not at risk. Code that bundled the browser build into a `<script>` tag was. 4.13.5 wrapped the loader in a `String.fromCharCode` obfuscator. 4.13.6 inlined the loader call in plaintext. The loader fetched `v3.jiathis.com/code/jia.js` from a compromised Chinese social-sharing CDN, pinged Baidu Analytics for every visitor, and checked the User-Agent for iPhone. For iPhone visitors it injected a zero-pixel iframe behind a closed Shadow DOM pointing at `utaq.cfww.shop/gooll/gooll.html` on 180.178.50.158, AS45753, Hong Kong. The iframe served a 50 KB fingerprinting loader that classified the device, beaconed every ten seconds to `l1ewsu3yjkqeroy.xyz/api/ip-sync/sync` behind Cloudflare, and content-addressed each follow-on module by `SHA256(sessionKey + moduleHash)[:40]` against the session key `cecd08aa6ff548c2`.

The final stage was the Coruna iOS exploit kit. Fourteen remote modules totaled roughly 606 KB. The kit chained 23 Safari and WebKit vulnerabilities and stopped at iOS 17.3, matching the CVE-2024-23222 patch for the `cassowary` JavaScriptCore type-confusion bug. The kit dispatched between ARM64 and ARM64_32 builds and ran a WebAssembly proof-of-work to confirm a real JavaScriptCore JIT rather than a sandbox. The terminal payload was a 31 KB native ARM64 shellcode dropper for the PLASMAGRID cryptocurrency-wallet implant. Anything outside Safari on iOS 13.0 to 17.2.1 received only the Baidu tracker. Socket attributed the deployment to UNC6691 at high confidence on Coruna kit fingerprints documented by Google's Threat Intelligence Group, the JiaThis hijack, the bulk-registered `.shop` domain pattern, the Baidu integration, and the Hong Kong AS45753 infrastructure.

Remediation is to pin `art-template` and its siblings to 4.13.2 or earlier and to audit CDN caches, bundler output, and downstream sites for references to `v3.jiathis.com`, `utaq.cfww.shop`, and `l1ewsu3yjkqeroy.xyz`. Socket's "Coruna respawned" framing reflects that the kit had gone quiet after Google TAG's earlier reporting on UNC6691. The novel piece in this incident is the delivery surface. The supply chain moved the kit off operator-controlled watering-hole domains and onto every downstream web app that bundled the browser build.
